thread:
maya-finops: Heads up  vendor "Silverpine Labs" submitted a W-8BEN but their email says they're a US sole proprietor and their invoice lists a US SSN. They asked to be paid ASAP. Should we accept the W-8 or ask for W-9?

chris-tax: If they're a US person (citizen/US resident/US entity) they must provide a W-9. W-8 is only for foreign persons. Using the wrong form can cause 1099 reporting gaps and backup withholding exposure.

olga-vendor: Hi, sorry for confusion. I'm Olga, I moved to the US last year but forgot to update vendor profile. I uploaded W-8 out of habit. Happy to upload a W-9.

acct-pay: Practical issues: we scheduled payment for 2026-03-05 for INV-2026-3320. If we need W-9, payment can be held until updated. Also if any backup withholding is required retroactively we'll need to handle adjustments.

compliance-bot: Vendor record note: SILVERPINE-VC updated 2026-02-27. Current tax doc on file: W-8BEN (uploaded 2026-02-26). No W-9 on file. Flag: US-person mismatch.

chris-tax: Steps: 1) Ask vendor to replace W-8 with a signed W-9. 2) If payment already made using incorrect form, assess whether backup withholding (24%) should have been applied. 3) If backup withholding would have applied and vendor disputes, require written request and any refunds to be coordinated via AP. 4) For 1099-MISC/NEC reporting, use the W-9 TIN once received for year-end.

maya-finops: Can we fast-track this? Vendor is small and urgent. Also, if we hold payment they might refuse work. Any temporary safe harbor?

chris-tax: We can accept a signed scanned W-9 via secure portal. Do not accept W-8 if they check US person. If they truly became US resident this tax year, W-9 is correct. For retro activity we need to check when status changed. If they were nonresident during the service period, W-8 may have been appropriate for that period. Ask vendor to state effective date of US residency.

olga-vendor: I became US resident 2026-01-10. Services were provided 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-20. I'll upload a signed W-9 now and note residency date.

acct-pay: Once W-9 is uploaded, we'll re-run pay-run eligibility. If payment is after residency date and W-9 present, no backup withholding. If our records show earlier residency or conflicting info, tax may request backup withholding until reconciled.

ledger-bot: Invoice recorded: INV-2026-3320 (vendor SILVERPINE-VC). Link: https://billing.redwood/invoices/INV-2026-3320

maya-finops: Request to vendor sent: "Please upload signed W-9 in vendor portal and confirm US residency effective date. If residency began before service dates, include a brief note. Payment will be processed after receipt."

olga-vendor: Uploaded W-9 and a short note confirming US residency since 2026-01-10. Sorry again!

chris-tax: Received. Next: 1) AP to clear payment if service dates fall after residency date. 2) If any payments already made under W-8, AP/Treasury to check for prior withholding. 3) Tax will annotate vendor record for 1099 filing. 4) Capture TIN verification screenshot (TIN matching) and keep audit trail.

acct-pay: Confirmed W-9 present. We'll process payment in the March run. Ticket FIN-5612 opened to document steps: vendor W-9, residency note, pay-run update, TIN validation screenshot.

maya-finops: Thanks. Can we add a check in vendor onboarding to flag email domain + country mismatch to avoid these? Small UX ask.

chris-tax: Good idea. Also store timestamp of tax-doc uploads and source IP for audit.

acct-pay: Noted. FIN-5612 will include a suggestion to add the onboarding flag. Closing thread once payment clears.
